standard_prerequisites.name: Dual pairs in a monoidal category and the two triangle identities
standard_prerequisites.use: Are unwound into the degreewise dual identities of part (3).

standard_prerequisites.name: Left duals of modules and the identification of the dual module with Hom_R(M, R)
standard_prerequisites.use: Gives part (2) and the identification used in the formula for the differential.

standard_prerequisites.name: The sign rule for the differential of a total complex
standard_prerequisites.use: Is what produces the factor -(-1)^n in the differential of the dual complex.

core_obligations: Unwind the two triangle identities (1 tensor epsilon) o (eta tensor 1) = id_{M^bullet} and (epsilon tensor 1) o (1 tensor eta) = id_{N^bullet} to extract the degreewise identities (1 tensor epsilon_n) o (eta_n tensor 1) = id_{M^n} and (epsilon_n tensor 1) o (1 tensor eta_n) = id_{N^{-n}}, which proves part (3) (proof lines 18494-18500).
Deduce part (2), that the terms are finite projective, from the one-module statement (proof line 18500).
Deduce part (1), that both complexes are bounded, from finiteness of the sum eta = sum eta_n (proof line 18501).

Since eta is a map of complexes R -> Tot(M^bullet tensor_R N^bullet), write down the identity (d_M^{-n-1} tensor 1) o eta_{-n-1} + (-1)^n (1 tensor d_N^{-n}) o eta_{-n} = 0 coming from the choice of signs for the total complex differential (proof lines 18502-18509).

Unwind the definitions in that identity to obtain the formula expressing d_N^n as -(-1)^n times the map induced by d_M^{-n-1} under the identification N^n = Hom_R(M^{-n}, R), proving part (4) (proof lines 18509).
Obtain the converse statement, the explicit construction of a left dual for a bounded complex of finite projective modules, by reading the above computation backwards (proof lines 18510-18511).
difficulty_reason: The lemma analyses a left dual (N^bullet, eta, epsilon) of a complex M^bullet in the monoidal category of complexes of R-modules, asserting four things: that M^bullet and N^bullet are bounded; that their terms are finite projective; that writing epsilon and eta as finite sums of degreewise components, each (N^{-n}, eta_n, epsilon_n) is the left dual of M^n in the sense of the one-module statement; and that the differential d_N^n equals -(-1)^n times the map induced by d_M^{-n-1} under the identification of N^n with Hom_R(M^{-n}, R). It also gives the converse construction (source lines 18461-18491). The proof unwinds the two triangle identities of a dual pair: from (1 tensor epsilon) o (eta tensor 1) = id and (epsilon tensor 1) o (1 tensor eta) = id it immediately extracts the degreewise identities (1 tensor epsilon_n) o (eta_n tensor 1) = id_{M^n} and (epsilon_n tensor 1) o (1 tensor eta_n) = id_{N^{-n}}, which proves part (3) (proof lines 18494-18500). Part (2) then follows from the one-module statement, and part (1) from the finiteness of the sum eta = sum eta_n (proof lines 18500-18501). The substantive part is (4): since eta is a map of complexes R -> Tot(M^bullet tensor_R N^bullet), the proof writes down the identity (d_M^{-n-1} tensor 1) o eta_{-n-1} + (-1)^n (1 tensor d_N^{-n}) o eta_{-n} = 0, which is exactly the sign rule for the total complex differential, and unwinding the definitions gives the claimed formula for d_N^n (proof lines 18502-18509). The converse is then obtained by reading the same computation backwards (proof lines 18510-18511). The non-routine content is the sign bookkeeping in the total complex that produces the twisted differential on the dual.
